summary: Hengelo's paid-parking area covers the centre and its edge car parks, with four garages or car parks listed by the municipality: the municipal garage De Beurs, garages Thiemsbrug and De Brink, and the station P+R at Gieskesstraat, which the municipality calls Q-Park P+R Station Hengelo and the national parking registry (a 2021 record, probably outdated) lists as an NS-operated P+R with 270 spaces, apparently the same site. There are more than 900 street spaces. Since 1 January 2026 the street tariff is 1.00 euro per 27 minutes (ordinance adopted by the council on 12 November 2025), with a day maximum of 8.80 euros at the day car parks, free street parking on Sundays and holidays, and a resident permit for the centre at 158.20 euros per year. Since January 2024 a 30-minute blue-zone replaces the Shop & Go spaces. Permit rules exclude addresses in the Binnenstad and Hart van Zuid development areas with a building permit granted after 29 September 2021 from resident permits. A 2019 count quoted in a 2021 municipal paper found the four garages together only 38 percent occupied at their busiest moment and street and open-lot parking about 50 percent occupied on average. In September 2024 the college decided to phase in paid parking in the ring around Hart van Zuid as housing is completed; only one street (De Clercqdwarsstraat) was confirmed in December 2024 for 1 January 2025, and the later status is not known. The council approved the Masterplan Lange Wemen on 17 December 2025; it would replace the Thiemsbrug garage with a public garage for about 430 cars, with construction of the first block expected to start at the end of 2027. Garage tariffs for Thiemsbrug, De Brink and the P+R come only from a municipal kermis booklet of June 2026 and were not checked against the operators.

items.text: A 2019 parking survey (Trajan, counts of October 2019), quoted in a consultant note in the municipality's 2021 parking-norms paper, found that on-street and open-lot spaces around the centre were on average about 50 percent occupied (about 40 percent on weekday daytimes, 58-60 percent on Saturday afternoon and shopping evening). The four garages are reported separately: at their busiest moment together 38 percent occupied with 835 spaces free, about 500 of them in De Brink and the station P+R garage; De Beurs reached 53 percent on a weekday evening with a theatre show and Thiemsbrug 62 percent on a Saturday afternoon. These are 2019 figures.
items.source_title: Parkeernormen Binnenstad en Hart van Zuid (version 23 Aug 2021, incl. Trajan 2019 data)

items.text: The Parkeerplan Hengelo of 2019 (a proposal paper, undated; PDF created August 2019) counted 3,216 paid-zone parking spaces, 1,351 of them in four garages: De Beurs 315, De Brink 377, Thiemsbrug 380 and the Station P+R 279. It expected ground-level capacity to fall by 254 spaces by 2023 because of developments, and reported the street tariff at 1.90 euros per hour, unchanged since 2010. To compensate for spaces to be lost on Burgemeester Jansenplein it prepared a new temporary lot at Kloosterhof (more than 100 spaces); a separate temporary lot at Marskant (54 spaces) had been opened in March 2019 for the duration of the works.

The 2019 Parkeerplan proposed four measures: a Shop & Go pilot of about 20 free 30-minute spaces, a 1-euro tariff from the third hour, paid hours aligned to shop hours (Mon-Fri 9-18, Sat 9-17, Thursday evening to 21:00) and a friendly-enforcement pilot with a first-time warning. A 2021 consultant note says the council adopted the plan with three measures: Shop & Go, aligned hours and friendly enforcement.
items.source_title: Parkeerplan Hengelo 2019 (PDF hosted by 1Twente); Parkeernormen Binnenstad en Hart van Zuid 2021

items.text: A 1Twente article (with RTV Oost) of 7 October 2022 reported that Hengelo was the only large city in Overijssel not raising its parking tariff, keeping 1.90 euros per hour. Alderman Hanneke Steen said that, with the centre under construction, she wanted to keep the current tariffs at least for that year. The article said Enschede would remain the most expensive from 1 January at 3.30 euros; Deventer (2.73 euros) and Zwolle (3.00 euros) were then still to decide on their increases. These are 2022 figures.
items.source_title: Alle Overijsselse steden verhogen parkeertarieven, behalve Hengelo (1Twente, 7 Oct 2022)

items.text: In September 2023 the college answered council questions from Lokaal Hengelo. Shop & Go was to end because its technology was not suitable for enforcement. The questions referred to raising the hourly tariff to 2.10 euros, and the college defended this by saying Hengelo's tariffs are low compared with Enschede, Almelo, Deventer, Zwolle and Emmen, and remain so after the increase. About two thirds of Hengelo residents cycle to the centre and 16 percent drive; about two thirds of the car visitors come from outside Hengelo. The college aims at a zero-emission centre by 2030 at the latest and said work on a new parking paper would start in Q2 2024.
items.source_title: Raadsvragen afschaffen Shop and Go en verhogen parkeertarieven (college answer, 5 Sep 2023)

items.text: On 5 December 2023 the college replaced the 13 Shop & Go spaces (in place since July 2020) with 13 blue-zone spaces with a 30-minute maximum from January 2024, as a temporary measure until the parking policy is updated, and set De Beurs garage at 0.50 euros per 14 minutes with a day maximum of 10.50 euros from 1 January 2024 (indexation under the Zomernota 2023-2027; the 7-euro evening tariff stayed).

On 10 September 2024 the college informed the council of its final decision to introduce paid parking in the ring around Hart van Zuid north of the Esrein, phased per sub-area as housing is completed, with the blue zone kept in the shopping area. After a six-week public inspection of the draft decision (21 February to 2 April 2024), about 2,800 addresses had been written to and 160 written responses (zienswijzen) were submitted. The council's principle decision on parking regulation dates from 29 September 2021; in 2021 the council set lower parking standards for the inner city and Hart van Zuid (at least 1,500 homes by 2030) with parking regulation as a condition, a steering rather than facilitating parking policy.
items.source_title: Definitief besluit parkeren schil Hart van Zuid (college letter, 10 Sep 2024)

items.text: On 26 November 2024 the college decided that paid parking with permits applies in De Clercqdwarsstraat (Hofmakerij project) from 1 January 2025, at the request of new residents; elsewhere in the Hart van Zuid ring, paid parking stays linked to completion of the Hart van Zuid projects.
items.source_title: Stand van zaken betaald parkeren schil Hart van Zuid (college letter, 4 Dec 2024)

items.text: On 30 September 2025 the college sent the Parkeerverordening 2026 and the parking tax ordinance 2026 to the council for adoption, proposing to remove the special e-charging permit from the parking ordinance; it adopted the Uitwerkingsbesluit Parkeerverordening 2026 itself, which states that nobody with parking on their own land gets a first resident permit. It also removed the e-charging exemption from the blue-zone rules and indexed the permits, subscriptions and exemptions in the De Beurs conditions 2026 by 4 percent in line with the Zomernota. Blue zones added in 2025 were Billiton- and Timorstraat and part of 't Wilbert (with part of Bornsestraat).

The Verordening parkeerbelastingen 2026, adopted by the council on 12 November 2025 and in force from 1 January 2026, sets the street and day-car-park tariff at 1.00 euro per 27 minutes, a day maximum of 8.80 euros at the five day car parks, and 0 euros with a disabled parking card. The resident permit for the centre area is 158.20 euros per year.
items.source_title: Verordening op de heffing en de invordering van parkeerbelastingen 2026 (CVDR747282)

items.text: The Uitwerkingsbesluit Parkeerverordening Hengelo 2026 (in force 1 January 2026) defines six permit areas with paid times Mon-Wed and Fri 9:00-18:00, Thursday 9:00-21:00 and Saturday 9:00-17:00, and issues no visitor permits in areas 1-3. Addresses in the inner-city and Hart van Zuid development areas with a building permit granted after 29 September 2021 get no resident or visitor permit.

The municipal page 'Parkeren in en om het centrum' (read 21 October 2026) lists 4 garages, more than 900 street spaces and 13 blue-zone spaces (free 30 minutes with a disc). The municipality itself runs garage De Beurs (0.50 euro per 14 minutes, 11.10 euros per 24 hours, 7 euros maximum 18:00-05:00); the other facilities are garages Thiemsbrug and De Brink and the Q-Park P+R Station Hengelo. Garages charge on Sundays and holidays, street parking does not.
items.source_title: Parkeren in en om het centrum (gemeente Hengelo)

items.text: The municipality's information booklet for the Lambertuskermis (16-20 September 2026; PDF produced in June 2026) lists, as parking information for visitors, garage Thiemsbrug at 1.80 euros per hour (maximum 14.00 euros per 24 hours, night tariff 3.00 euros from 18:00 to 05:00, open 08:00-22:00 with no exit outside those hours), garage De Brink at 1.00 euro per 22 minutes (maximum 11.00 euros per day) and the 'Q-park P+R Station Hengelo' car park at Gieskesstraat at 2.19 euros per 60 minutes with a 10.50 euro daily maximum. The tariffs were not checked against operator pages.

Permit prices (read 21 October 2026): the 'algemeen Centrum' permit costs 72.40 euros per month (minimum one month; at least three months to get access to garage De Beurs with a pass) and the permit for the day car parks 173.50 euros per year. Centre residents pay 158.20 euros per year and can use De Beurs with an access pass; a resident needs a car registered at their name and address, no parking space of their own (or at most one if they have several cars) and no space to rent or buy in their complex, and the address must not be in the Binnenstad or Hart van Zuid development areas.
items.source_title: Parkeervergunning algemeen and Parkeervergunning voor bewoners (gemeente Hengelo)

items.text: The conditions for garage De Beurs (in force from 1 January 2026) say that licence-plate recognition is used at the barriers and for subscription holders (a pass is issued if a plate is not recognised), that the garage is open 24 hours a day with speed gates closed between 18:00 and 08:00, and that the maximum vehicle height is 2.00 m.
items.source_title: Algemene voorwaarden en regels parkeergarage De Beurs (CVDR745524)

items.text: The national parking data registry (RDW NPR, read 21 October 2026) lists 'P+R Industrieplein (Hengelo)' at Gieskesstraat with 270 spaces, 2.1 m minimum height, no charging points, open 24/7, operator Nederlandse Spoorwegen, tariff text 2.05 euros per hour (record dating from June 2021, so probably outdated). The municipality's pages list a 'Q-Park P+R Station Hengelo' on Gieskesstraat, apparently the same site (279 spaces in the 2019 plan).

Hengelo's charging page (read 21 October 2026) says the municipality tries to place a public charger within 250 metres of every resident. Residents who own or are about to own an electric car, have no parking space of their own and no charger within 250 metres can request one; Vattenfall assesses the request and places and manages the charger. Two parking spaces are reserved per charger by default. Where the space lies in a paid-parking area or garage and the user has no parking permit, parking fees are due in addition to the charging cost. The Laadpalenkaart was adopted in 2022.

The council unanimously approved the Masterplan Lange Wemen on 17 December 2025 and the college signed an anterior agreement with VanWonen (decision of 26 May 2026). The plan has about 310 homes and a public garage for about 430 cars plus 500-750 bicycle spaces, replacing the Thiemsbrug garage; the college said in 2022 it is a replacement, with the Kloosterhof lot, not an extra garage. Construction of the first block was expected to start end of 2027.
items.source_title: Gemeentenieuws 18 Nov 2025; Openbare besluiten B&W 7 juli 2026; college answer 6 Dec 2022

gaps: Q-Park Hengelo pages (garage De Brink, P+R) could not be opened (404) and no Q-Park or NS operator tariff page was read; Brink, Thiemsbrug and P+R tariffs rest on the municipal Lambertuskermis booklet, and the P+R tariff in the RDW record dates from 2021.
No Tubantia, RTV Oost or 1Twente article from 2024-2026 on city-centre parking was found or opened; only a 1Twente/RTV Oost article of October 2022 was read. Tubantia was not searched directly.

The municipal permit page lists 80.50 euros per year for Thiemsland, Tuindorp and Weidedorp residents, while the 2026 tariff table (CVDR747282) lists 41.10 euros (extra cars 123.50) for areas 4 and 6; the discrepancy is unresolved, so those prices are not stated in items.

The promised new parking policy paper (parkeernota, work due to start Q2 2024) and any council decision on it were not found; the Zomernota 2023 and 2025 themselves, the Trajan parking survey report and any post-2019 occupancy data were not opened.

No source found for current garage occupancy, a parking guidance or open-data system for the centre, or the status of the Hart van Zuid mobility hub and paid parking in the Hart van Zuid ring after December 2024.

The centrumparkeren.nl portal (2025 tariffs of 2.10 euros per hour) was opened but not used because it is a parking-listing portal and conflicts with the official 2026 tariff of 1.00 euro per 27 minutes.
